'''Melanie Georgina Lee''' [[CBE]] (born 29 July 1958)<ref name=lundbeck>{{cite web|url=http://investor.lundbeck.com/releasedetail.cfm?ReleaseID=653052|title=Notice of Annual General Meeting|work=Lundbeck|date=1 March 2012|accessdate=14 September 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171206160330/http://investor.lundbeck.com/releasedetail.cfm?releaseid=653052|archive-date=6 December 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> is an English pharmaceutical industry executive and CEO of [[Medical Research Council Technology|LifeArc]], succeeding Dave Tapolczay in November 2018.

==Career==

===Research===
{{quotebox|align=right|width=25%|bgcolor=#c6dbf7|quote="Paul and Melanie's paper started a revolution in cell cycle research."|source=Kathleen Weston<ref name=blue/>}}
Lee received an undergraduate degree in Biology from the [[University of York]], working with Simon Hardy,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.york.ac.uk/news-and-events/news/2009/plant-biologist-honoured/|title=Honour for University of York plant biologist|publisher=University of York| date=2 January 2009|accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref> and then a PhD at [[National Institute for Medical Research]] in London.<ref name=expert>{{cite news|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/watching-expert-becoming-expert|title=From Watching 'The Expert' to Becoming An Expert|last=Cahoon|first=Lauren|work=Science Magazine|date=26 September 2008|accessdate=14 September 2015|doi=10.1126/science.caredit.a0800142}}</ref>

Lee worked as a [[molecular genetics]] postdoc, first at [[Imperial College London]] on yeast and then from 1985 with [[Paul Nurse]] at the [[Imperial Cancer Research Fund|ICRF]]'s [[London Research Institute#Lincoln.27s Inn Fields laboratories|Lincoln's Inn Laboratories]].<ref name=blue>{{cite book|chapter-url=http://blueskiesbenchspace.org/index.php?pag=6|title=Blue Skies and Bench Space|chapter=6: Divide and Rule|last=Weston|first=Kathleen|publisher=Cancer Research UK|accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref> Nurse's work on the [[cell cycle]] won him the Nobel Prize, and in his speech he cited Lee's work on finding a human homologue of the yeast gene [[cdc2]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bioscience.jbpub.com/cells/EXP82.aspx|title=The discovery of cdc2 as the key regulator of the cell cycle|last=Nurse|first=Paul|work=Cells|publisher=Jones and Bartlett Publishers|year=2007|accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref> Nurse said of this work that "I suppose the most astonishing thing was the way Melanie Lee in the lab did it by complementation."<ref>{{cite journal|pmc=2650208|title=The cell cycle and beyond: an interview with Paul Nurse|journal=Disease Models & Mechanisms|last=Smith|first=Jim|date=March 2009|pmid=19259383|doi=10.1242/dmm.002592|doi-access=free|volume=2|issue=3–4|pages=113–5}}</ref> Lee later recounted being uncomfortable with the competition in the laboratory.<ref name=expert/>

In 2003, she was elected a Fellow of the [[Academy of Medical Sciences]].<ref>[http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/dr-melanie-lee/ Dr Melanie Lee CBE FMedSci], Academy of Medical Sciences. Retrieved 4 March 2014</ref>

===Works===
* {{cite journal|title=Complementation used to clone a human homologue of the fission yeast cell cycle control gene cdc2|first1=Melanie G.|last1=Lee|first2=Paul|last2=Nurse|journal=Nature|volume=327|issue=6117|pages=31–5|date=7 May 1987|doi=10.1038/327031a0|pmid=3553962|bibcode=1987Natur.327...31L|s2cid=4300190 }}

===Business===
Lee was appointed [[chief executive officer]] of [[Medical Research Council Technology|LifeArc]] in November 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.lifearc.org/new-ceo-appointment/|title=LifeArc announces new CEO appointment|date=2018-09-04|website=LifeArc|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref> Lee currently serves on the Board of Directors at [[Sanofi]] and on the Board of Trustees at the Dementia Research Institute. Previously, she was [[chief scientific officer]] of [[BTG plc|BGT Plc]] and was the founder and CEO of NightstaRx, a [[Syncona]], [[Wellcome Trust]] company in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Melanie Lee|url=https://www.lifescienceintegrates.com/melanie-lee/|website=Life Science Integrates|language=en-GB|access-date=2020-05-14}}</ref>

She began her pharmaceutical industry career at [[Glaxo]] in 1988, leaving academia after she became pregnant. She joined [[Celltech]] in 1998 where she was Director of R&D.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/Research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=512174&privcapId=127549|work=BloombergBusiness|title=Melanie G. Lee CBE, PhD, FMedSci, DSc (Hons)|accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref> She held the same role at [[UCB Pharmaceuticals]] and was CEO of Syntaxin Ltd from 2010 to 2013.<ref name="expert" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/fellows/fellows-directory/ordinary-fellows/dr-melanie-lee/|title=Dr Melanie Lee CBE FMedSci|work=The Academy of Medical Sciences|accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.mednous.com/appointment/melanie-lee-becomes-ceo-syntaxin|title=Melanie Lee becomes CEO of Syntaxin|work=MedNous|publisher=Evernow Publishing|date=8 February 2010|accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref> She had Chair and Deputy Chair Trustee appointments at Cancer Research Technology and [[Cancer Research UK]] respectively. She was on the board of Lundbeck<ref name="lundbeck" /> and founded the Think10 business advice company.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.think10.eu/about-us.html|title=About us|work=Think10|accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref>

She was an advisor to the 2014–15 [[Ann Dowling|Dowling]] Review of business-university research collaborations.<ref name=dowling>{{cite web|url=http://www.raeng.org.uk/policy/dowling-review/dowling-review-steering-group#Melanie-Lee|title=Dowling Review Group|work=Royal Academy of Engineering|accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref>

==Awards==
In January 2019, Lee was awarded the BIA Lifetime Achievement Award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.bioindustry.org/news-listing/melanie-lee-cbe-bia-lifetime-achievement-award-winner-2019.html|title=Melanie Lee CBE {{!}} BIA Lifetime Achievement Award Winner 2019|last=BIA|website=www.bioindustry.org|access-date=2019-03-30}}</ref> She received a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire|CBE]] in 2009 in respect of her for services to medical science<ref>[http://www.cancertechnology.co.uk/dr-melanie-lee-chairman-crt-awarded-commander-order-british-empire-cbe Dr. Melanie Lee, Chairman of CRT, is awarded Commander of the Order of the British Empire (CBE)], Cancer Research Technology. Retrieved 4 March 2014</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2008/dec/30/new-years-honours-list-dbe-and-cbe|title=New Year honours list: DBEs and CBEs|date=31 December 2008|work=The Guardian|accessdate=14 September 2015}}</ref> and in 2014, she was named as one of the top 100 "leading practising scientists" in the UK by the [[Science Council]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.co.uk/news/the-uks-100-leading-practising-scientists/2010580.article|title=The UK's 100 leading practising scientists|date=17 January 2014|accessdate=14 September 2015|work=Times Higher Education}}</ref>

==Personal life==
She is married to Christopher, with whom she lives in London. They have two sons.<ref name=expert/>
